test_title: PYST 58: SSC CPO - English Comprehension (Held  on 27 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: english
question: What does the expression “drill into your heads” mean?

options.text: make someone learn or understand something by repeating it
force someone to move his/her head in a particular direction
repeatedly question someone regarding a certain issue

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Explanation:** The expression "**drill into your heads**" means **to make someone learn or understand something by repeating it**.
 
• This phrase is often used when someone** is trying to emphasize the importance of a particular piece of information or a concept by repeating it multiple times until it is well understood**.
 
• In this context of the paragraph this **idiomatic expression** perfectly signifies the meaning which states to** make someone learn or understand something by repeating it.**

Hence the correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Why the other options are incorrect:**

 
 
• **Threaten someone repeatedly with a drill machine:** This option is** incorrect** because the expression **does not imply **any physical threat or the use of a drill machine.
 
• **Force someone to move his/her head in a particular direction:** This option is** incorrect **as the expression is** metaphorical and does not involve any** physical movement of the head.
 
• **Repeatedly question someone regarding a certain issue:** Although this option involves repetition, it **does not capture** the essence of making someone learn or understand something through repetition, which is the primary meaning of the expression.
